about.title: About Life Insurance Calculator - Coverage Needs Assessment Tool
about.description: The Life Insurance Calculator is a comprehensive financial planning tool designed to help you determine the appropriate amount of life insurance coverage needed to protect your family's financial future. This calculator analyzes your income, debts, expenses, and financial goals to recommend optimal coverage amounts. Whether you're buying your first policy or reviewing existing coverage, this tool provides personalized life insurance needs analysis.

howTo.title: How to Use the Life Insurance Calculator

steps.title: Enter Personal Information
steps.description: Input your age, gender, health status, and smoking status for accurate calculations.

steps.title: Add Income Details
steps.description: Enter your annual income and number of years your family would need income replacement.

steps.title: List Outstanding Debts
steps.description: Include mortgage balance, credit cards, loans, and other debts to be covered.

steps.title: Calculate Future Expenses
steps.description: Add children's education costs, funeral expenses, and other future financial needs.

steps.title: Consider Existing Assets
steps.description: Subtract current savings, investments, and existing life insurance coverage.

steps.title: Review Coverage Recommendation
steps.description: Analyze the recommended coverage amount and compare policy types.

faq.q: How much life insurance do I need?
faq.a: A common rule is 10-12 times your annual income, but actual needs depend on debts, dependents, income replacement years, and financial goals. Our calculator provides personalized recommendations based on your specific situation.

faq.q: What's the difference between term and whole life insurance?
faq.a: Term life provides coverage for a specific period (10-30 years) at lower cost. Whole life provides permanent coverage with cash value but costs significantly more. Term is often better for temporary needs like mortgage protection.

faq.q: When should I review my life insurance coverage?
faq.a: Review coverage after major life events: marriage, divorce, birth of children, home purchase, job changes, or every 3-5 years. Your insurance needs change as your financial situation evolves.

faq.q: Can I have too much life insurance?
faq.a: While there's no legal limit, having excessive coverage means paying unnecessary premiums. Focus on covering actual financial needs: income replacement, debt payoff, and future expenses like education costs.
